_comment: One row per upstream. tier: 1 = official statistical agency / regulator primary data, 2 = official aggregator republishing tier-1 data, 3 = reputable secondary. reliability_score is the base 0-100 used in scoring before fetch-failure penalties. cadence_minutes is the default poll interval for this source's series; a series row may override it. key_env names the env var holding an API key: required_key=true means the adapter skips (and logs) when it is missing.

purged_sources.reason: DefiLlama terms forbid commercial use and republishing of its data without permission. All stored DefiLlama data is deleted on the Pi and the hub.

sources.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.notes: Uses the JSON API when FRED_API_KEY is set, otherwise the public fredgraph.csv download. Some FRED series carry third-party copyright; the catalog only lists public-domain government series.

sources.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API
sources.notes: v2 with a key (500 queries/day, 50 series each); v1 without (25 queries/day, 25 series each). Series are batched into one request per 25.

sources.name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis API
sources.notes: Free UserID required. Slow series: weekly poll is enough; quarterly releases.

sources.name: SEC EDGAR (submissions and XBRL company facts)
sources.notes: No key, but SEC fair access requires a User-Agent naming the operator and a contact email (set PMIC_SEC_USER_AGENT) and at most 10 requests/second. Requests are spaced 150 ms apart.

sources.name: openFDA (drug enforcement, drugs@FDA, FAERS)
sources.notes: 1,000 requests/day without a key, 120,000 with. FAERS adverse event reports are unverified voluntary reports; counts are an attention/safety proxy, not incidence. openFDA is not for clinical decisions.

sources.name: World Bank Indicators API v2
sources.notes: CC BY 4.0. Annual series, weekly poll.

sources.name: European Central Bank Data Portal (SDMX API)
sources.notes: Free, no key. ECB statistics may be reused with the source cited. CSV (csvdata) per series key.

sources.name: FDIC BankFind Suite API (bank failures)
sources.notes: Free, no key. US government work. Failures are rare, so counts are quarterly over ten years.

sources.name: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database API
sources.notes: Free, no key. Complaints are not verified by the CFPB and volume reflects awareness as well as problems; read counts as a stress proxy.

sources.name: Wikimedia REST API (pageviews and edits)
sources.notes: Free, no key; requests carry a User-Agent with a contact URL per Wikimedia's policy. Data CC0. Human users only (agent=user).

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (NIH National Library of Medicine)
sources.notes: Free, no key, about 50 requests a minute. Registry data entered by sponsors.

sources.name: CPSC Recalls API (SaferProducts.gov)
sources.notes: Free, no key. Units come from each recall's NumberOfUnits text ("About 12,000") and are approximate.

sources.name: NHTSA recalls (U.S. DOT open data, Socrata dataset 6axg-epim)
sources.notes: Free, no key (anonymous Socrata rate limits). Vehicle, equipment, tire and child seat recalls by report received date.

sources.name: OpenFEC API (Federal Election Commission)
sources.notes: Free key from api.data.gov (email only). Without one the collector uses DEMO_KEY (about 50 requests a day), which is enough for the weekly poll.

sources.name: U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act API
sources.notes: Free; works without a key at a low rate limit (requests are spaced 4 s apart). An optional free key raises it.

sources.name: USAspending.gov API (U.S. Treasury)
sources.notes: Free, no key. Award obligations by month; the latest months fill in as agencies report (Defense with a delay), so they are revised upward.

sources.name: World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet)
sources.notes: CC BY 4.0. Monthly averages from the CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx workbook; the link is read from the Pink Sheet page each poll because it changes with every release.

sources.name: TreasuryDirect auction results (Bureau of the Fiscal Service)
sources.notes: Free, no key. Note and Bond auctions; monthly means of bid-to-cover, bidder shares and the high-minus-median yield spread.

sources.name: OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries v2
sources.notes: Free, no key. Rows are per designated area; declarations are counted once per disaster number.

sources.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (FDSN event service)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Monthly counts by magnitude; the US box includes nearby parts of Canada and Mexico.

sources.name: National Weather Service alerts API (api.weather.gov)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key, User-Agent required. Active alerts only, so the series is a daily snapshot that builds history from the first run.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. One JSON file; additions counted by dateAdded.

sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database (CVE API 2.0)
sources.notes: Free. Without a key, 5 requests per 30 s, so a full backfill takes a few minutes; a free key makes it about ten times faster. Weekly poll.

sources.name: CDC National Syndromic Surveillance Program (data.cdc.gov)
sources.notes: Public domain. Socrata API; an app token is optional and only raises rate limits.

sources.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, petroleum weekly history
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Reads the dnav history table for each series; FRED no longer serves these weekly stock and refinery series.

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Formation Statistics
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. One monthly CSV; US totals, seasonally adjusted. FRED does not serve these ids.

sources.name: Pocket Network indexer (data.pocket.network GraphQL)
sources.notes: Free, no key. Weekly sums of estimated (throughput) and claimed relays, staked supplier and app counts on each week's last block.

sources.name: National Interagency Fire Center, WFIGS incident locations
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Monthly wildfire incidents and acres (as last reported; recent months revise upward).

sources.name: NOAA NCEI Climate at a Glance (national)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Contiguous US monthly temperature and precipitation departures from the 1991-2020 normal. Weekly poll.

sources.name: TSA checkpoint travel numbers
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Daily passengers screened, summed into weeks.

sources.name: IMF World Economic Outlook (SDMX data API)
sources.notes: Free, no key (api.imf.org). Annual values with IMF projections; kept up to next year. Weekly poll; WEO updates twice a year.

sources.name: Federal Register API (National Archives)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Monthly counts of final, proposed and significant rules.

sources.name: CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment (data.cms.gov)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. National Medicare beneficiaries by month: total, Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage. Weekly poll.

sources.name: SEC fails-to-deliver data
sources.notes: Public domain; SEC fair access needs a User-Agent with contact (PMIC_SEC_USER_AGENT). Half-monthly zips summed per company and month as dollar value. Weekly poll.

sources.name: BLS and BEA release calendars (iCalendar)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Scheduled release dates from the BLS and BEA calendar feeds, kept as events; the number of major releases in the next 30 days is a daily snapshot.

sources.name: OECD Data Explorer (SDMX API)
sources.notes: Free, no key; OECD data is CC BY 4.0. Composite leading indicators, monthly; one request per run. Business and consumer confidence are left out because some countries' series are built from licensed surveys.

sources.name: FDA warning letters (fda.gov listing)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. The warning letter table behind fda.gov's listing page, paged newest first; monthly counts by posted date and drug or device letters as events.

sources.name: Congress.gov API (Library of Congress)
sources.notes: Free api.data.gov key (CONGRESS_API_KEY, falls back to FEC_API_KEY). Without a key only laws are collected: DEMO_KEY allows 10 requests an hour, too few to page every bill. Bills introduced and public laws enacted, monthly. Weekly poll.

sources.name: EPA ECHO enforcement case services
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. Civil enforcement cases with a milestone in each month, those with a federal penalty, judicial cases, and the penalties assessed. Recent months fill in as cases are entered. Daily poll: finished months are kept, so a pass cut short by a rate limit carries on the next day.

sources.name: IRS SOI exempt organization extracts (Form 990)
sources.notes: Public domain, no key. One zip per processing year (about 55 MB); each year is read once, streamed, and summed; the zip itself is not kept. Weekly check for a new year.

sources.name: SEC Form 13F data sets
sources.notes: Public domain; SEC fair access needs the User-Agent in PMIC_SEC_USER_AGENT. One zip per filing window (about 85 MB); each window is read once, streamed for the 14 companies' CUSIPs, and not kept. Weekly check for a new window.
